title: Druidy druids
html_source: Druids were the priesthood in the pre-Christian pagan religion of Celtic Ireland and Britain. They are referred to several times in the book, usually by Mulligan, as a byword for traditional Gaelic culture which at the time was in the process of being reconstructed by proponents of the Celtic Revival such as W.B. Yeats. This movement believed that a return to Gaelic pagan traditions could be used to inspire pride in indigenous Irish culture, and thus help the cause of Irish independence. However very little of the Druids' beliefs can be known for certain since they left no written records, but their legacy remains in physical artifacts, most famously Stonehenge in England. Buck Mulligan seems skeptical of the Celtic Revival, later in the chapter characterizing the movement’s books as “ten pages of notes about the folk and the fishgods of Dundrum”.
